title: Common-quotient tower presentations and local ideal-product membership
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, let $R,B$ be sheaves of commutative rings, and let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a homomorphism. A common-quotient tower presentation consists of an inverse system $S:\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,\operatorname{CommRing})$ [def-weil-inverse-system] and natural transformations $q:\operatorname{const}R\to S$ and $b:\operatorname{const}B\to S$. Require each $q_n$ to be locally surjective and each square with top arrow $\varphi$, left arrow $q_n$, right arrow $b_n$ and bottom arrow $\operatorname{id}_{S_n}$ to be a pushout in commutative ring sheaves. Thus $S_n$ is the sheaf quotient of $R$ by the kernel ideal sheaf $I_n=\ker(q_n)$ and simultaneously the quotient of $B$ by the extended ideal $I_nB$, with the identification induced by $\varphi$; naturality records all quotient transitions. Index $n=0$ denotes the first quotient. Define $I_n(U)=\ker(R(U)\to S_n(U))$. For an $R$-module sheaf $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define local membership of $x\in M(U)$ in $I_nM$ by the requirement that the sieve generated by arrows $f:V\to U$ for which $x|_V$ lies in the $R(V)$-submodule spanned by $\{jp:j\in I_n(V),\ p\in M(V)\}$ is a covering sieve.
